GitHub Copilot in Teams: a 7-slide test plan for turning a bug report into a reviewed fix.

What changed: GitHub's October 23 update brings notifications and Copilot together in the new GitHub app for Microsoft Teams.

What it does: mention @GitHub on an issue notification to investigate the bug, propose a fix and create a pull request. Your team still reviews, tests and merges.

Why builders should care: the conversation can carry the context into the build, instead of becoming another place where work stalls.

Try this week:
1. Install or update the consolidated GitHub app in Teams. Connect your account and select a test repository when prompted.
2. Use one small bug with exact reproduction steps, expected behavior and a clear acceptance check.
3. Mention @GitHub to investigate and propose the fix.
4. Read the diff, run the relevant tests and verify the original bug before deciding whether to merge.

Signal: AI is moving from answering the conversation to participating in the workflow. The acceptance standard stays human.

On Tech Thursday, our CLI-to-image connection worked while the first images still fell short. Different tool surface; the same reason to separate execution from acceptance.

Save this for your next AI-assisted bug fix.

slides.openai_prompt: Create a cinematic Layer8Culture visual in a deep black environment with electric blue accent lighting, premium creator-tech atmosphere, late-night builder energy, documentary realism, human-centered AI themes, Black tech futurism, minimal composition, strong negative space, warm practical lighting, and high contrast. Vary the composition from post to post so the feed does not repeat - the SCENE SPECIFICS for THIS post decide the subject. Draw from a range of premium looks (do NOT default to the same person-at-a-desk shot every time), for example: a confident Black creator/host presenting direct-to-camera; a close detail of premium creator gear (mic, stream deck, dark walnut desk, the standalone 8 motif on a hoodie or mug); an over-the-shoulder build session; an abstract Afrofuturistic tech or data-visualization environment with glowing electric-blue nodes and grids; or an atmospheric branded studio space. Recurring brand cues when a scene fits: a blank neon sign panel on the wall (an unlit, lettering-free glowing panel - do NOT render any text or letters), the standalone 8 motif, a bookshelf washed in blue accent lighting. When a person appears they are a confident Black creator, engaged and intentional, never anonymous side profiles. The image should feel like a premium technology documentary and creative studio brand. COMPOSITION FOR TYPOGRAPHY: leave the LOWER-LEFT / lower third of the frame as clean, uncluttered negative space (a dark, simple area with no faces, fine detail, or busy elements there) so a branded headline can be composited over it. Add-on: Editorial Drop judgment metaphor, square photographic still, no person. Scene: a precision balance suspended in the upper-right of a dark architectural alcove; one pan carries a small blue machined part, the other a soft-white physical calibration weight, showing deliberate evaluation rather than speed. Fine warm practical reflection on brushed metal, 75 percent black/navy, restrained electric blue only. Quiet dark lower third for headline, no decorative symbols or labels. Avoid generic startup office, bright corporate lighting, cheap gamer RGB, cluttered composition, cartoon props, excessive sci-fi armor, robots, fake hologram overload, random neon colors, copyrighted franchise references, garbled screen text, random figurines, tripod-mounted monitors, makeshift setups, rendered text, signage lettering, and garbled typography.
